title: PortSwigger Burp Suite Certified Practitioner
summary: The Burp Suite Certified Practitioner exam, code BSCP, is a four hour practical web security certification from PortSwigger, the company behind the Burp Suite testing tool. It is aimed at penetration testers, application security engineers and bug bounty hunters who already work through web vulnerability classes confidently and now want independent proof. The exam gives you two deliberately vulnerable applications, each solved in three stages: get into any user account, reach the admin interface, then read a specific file from the server's filesystem. You must hold an active Burp Suite Professional licence, test unaided, and hand in your Burp project file for analysis. It proves to an employer that you can chain separate flaws into a working exploit and explain the impact. It leads to roles such as application security analyst, penetration tester and security consultant. PortSwigger publishes no numbered exam domains, so the chapters below follow its published exam process and the skills it names for preparation, not a vendor syllabus. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by PortSwigger.

beginner.definition: This is a practical exam from PortSwigger that tests whether you can find and use weaknesses in real web applications. Burp Suite is a tool that sits between your browser and a website so that you can read and change the traffic. The certification shows you can use that tool, plus your own knowledge, to break into deliberately vulnerable practice sites. It is not a multiple choice quiz.
beginner.whyItMatters: Web applications are where most attackers get in, so companies pay well for people who can test them properly. A written exam shows that you remember facts, but this exam shows that you can find a real flaw in a running system within a time limit. That makes your result believable to an employer who has been disappointed by candidates who only passed a quiz. It is a strong step toward a penetration testing or application security career, and it stays valid for several years once earned.
howItWorks: Learn the core web vulnerability classes first, using the free online labs from the same vendor, such as cross site scripting, which is injecting script into a page that other users will view.
Practise with Burp Suite every day until reading and editing requests in the proxy feels as natural as using a browser.
Solve every apprentice and practitioner level lab in each topic without opening the offered solution, then write short notes on the cause and the fix.
Use mystery labs, which give you no clue about the vulnerability type, because the exam does not label anything for you.
Practise chaining flaws together, since each exam application needs three linked steps rather than one isolated trick.
Take a practice exam to rehearse the clock, then read the vendor's exam hints before you book the real thing.
beginner.example: Think of a website as a hotel with many doors. A normal user walks in the front entrance and goes to their room. A tester tries the fire exit, the staff lift and the window on the second floor. One small gap, such as a window left open for the cleaner, may be enough to get in. The exam then asks for more than entry. You must reach the manager's office using that first foot in the door, and finally open the safe inside. Each step uses a different weakness, and you have four hours to link all three.
takeaways: You cannot pass by memorising answers, so budget many hours of hands on lab practice before booking.
You must own an active Burp Suite Professional licence, because the exam cannot be completed without it.
PortSwigger publishes no domain list, so treat the Web Security Academy topic list as your syllabus and check the current exam guidance before booking.

objectives: Intercept, inspect and modify web traffic with a proxy tool during a live test
Identify and exploit common injection, authentication and access control weaknesses in running applications
Chain two or more separate flaws together to reach a goal that neither flaw allows on its own
Escalate a foothold on the server side in order to read files or run commands
Deliver an attack that another user or an administrator will trigger in their own session
Work methodically against unlabelled targets and keep a clean record of the testing process
attributionNote: PortSwigger certification content is an independent study guide written for CyberPulseAcademy from the publicly published exam objectives. It is NOT official PortSwigger material. CyberPulseAcademy is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by PortSwigger. Always check the vendor's current objectives before you book an exam.

chapters.title: Reconnaissance and attack surface mapping
objectives: Enumerate content, parameters and accounts before attempting any attack
Work out the technologies in use from responses, headers and error messages
Spot username enumeration and other information leaks that widen the attack surface
Choose between manual testing and targeted scanning for each part of an application
Keep a reliable record of everything tested so that no lead is lost

chapters.title: Gaining access to a user account
objectives: Exploit authentication logic flaws in password reset, multi factor checks and remember me cookies
Break into an account through injection in a login form or through predictable session tokens
Abuse token and single sign on mechanisms such as weak signature checks and forced account linking
Escalate a discovered username into a valid session using enumeration and careful brute force
Recognise when a small logic error is enough to bypass a control entirely

chapters.title: Privilege escalation to the admin interface
objectives: Find admin functionality that is hidden rather than properly protected
Break access control that relies on a request parameter, a header or the request method
Abuse insecure direct object references to reach another user's data or role
Cause an administrator's browser to perform an action on your behalf
Use server side flaws such as prototype pollution or cache poisoning to gain elevated rights

chapters.title: Reading files and running code on the server
objectives: Exploit file path traversal to read files outside the intended directory
Use template injection or insecure deserialisation to reach code execution
Retrieve files or internal responses through server side request forgery
Inject operating system commands where user input reaches a shell
Turn a blind or out of band condition into proof that the attack worked

chapters.title: Cross user attack delivery
objectives: Store a payload that another user will load in their own authenticated session
Bypass content security policy and other client side defences
Deliver an attack through cache poisoning or request smuggling when direct delivery fails
Use an exploit server to send a target to a malicious page you control
Confirm a cross user attack fired and capture what it returned

chapters.title: Encodings, filters and defence evasion
objectives: Encode a payload correctly for the context in which it is decoded
Bypass blacklist and whitelist filters that block obvious attack strings
Use alternative syntax and case variation when a filter is too narrow
Work out where in the request a blocked value is being inspected
Adjust a failing payload step by step instead of starting again

chapters.title: Burp Suite workflow and exam conduct
objectives: Drive the proxy, repeater, intruder and collaborator tools fluently under time pressure
Automate re authentication with session handling rules so long attacks survive a logout
Use targeted scanning during manual testing to find leads quickly
Maintain a tidy Burp project file, because the project file is submitted and analysed
Work unaided and within the rules, since sharing addresses or accepting help ends the certification
